QuestionStmt.S: Identify from following the conjugate base of $$\mathrm{[Zn(H_2O)_4]^{2+}}$$

Solution.S:
The conjugate base is formed when an acid loses one proton, H⁺.

Here the complex is $\mathrm{Zn(H_2O)_4^{2+}}$.

One coordinated water molecule, H₂O, can lose H⁺ and become OH⁻.

So,

$$\mathrm{Zn(H_2O)_4^{2+} \rightarrow [Zn(H_2O)_3OH]^+ + H^+}$$

The charge also matches: the original complex has charge +2. After losing H⁺, the conjugate base has charge +1.

Thus, the conjugate base is $\mathrm{Zn(H_2O)_3OH^+}$.

Final Answer: $$\boxed{\mathrm{Zn(H_2O)_3OH^+}}$$

Hence, the correct option is C.
